questions.q: What fundamentally distinguishes data blending from a relationship or a join?
options: Blending never combines the data itself — each source is queried and aggregated independently, then the results are stitched together only in the visualization
Blending is just another name for a relationship
Blending only works with Excel files
Blending requires writing custom SQL, unlike joins
questions.explain: A blend runs two separate queries, aggregates each independently, and lines up the aggregated results by a shared field — no single combined table is ever created, unlike a join or relationship.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when are you forced to use a blend instead of a relationship or join?
options: When one source is a published Tableau data source, when the connectors are incompatible for cross-database joins, or when linking fields need to vary sheet by sheet
Whenever you're using an Excel file as one of your sources
Only when you have more than 10 tables
Blending is always preferred over relationships
questions.explain: Blending is a fallback for cases relationships and joins can't handle: published data sources, incompatible connectors, or per-sheet linking field flexibility.

questions.q: What is the 'primary' data source in a blend?
options: The first data source added to the worksheet — its fields drive the view
Whichever data source has more rows
The data source connected via a live connection rather than an extract
There is no distinction between primary and secondary in a blend
questions.explain: The primary data source is the one whose fields build the base of the view; the secondary source is blended in and linked by shared fields.

questions.q: What do you do when the linking field names don't match between the primary and secondary data source?
options: Manually map them using the Add/Edit Field Mapping dialog
Blending is impossible unless field names match exactly
Rename every field in the underlying database
Convert the secondary source into a Tableau extract first
questions.explain: The Add/Edit Field Mapping dialog lets you pick the primary field and the corresponding secondary field manually when names differ.

questions.q: What is the real limitation of data blending compared to a relationship or join?
options: You can't do row-level analysis across the two sources — the secondary source's measures are already aggregated by the time they reach the view
Blending only supports one data source at a time
Blending can't use any filters
Blending is slower than a join in every case
questions.explain: Because each source is aggregated independently before being stitched together, a blend can't combine data at the row level — that requires a relationship or join instead.
